findings.claim: The selftest fixture isolation architecture is non-viable for the 020C transition: both policy-check.yml invocations (fixture-pass-policy-check and fixture-fail-policy-check) receive identical PR context and produce identical summaries. When 020C adds Rego rules and updates fixture-fail/services.yml with a deliberate violation, both invocations will produce deny findings; the comparison of the first invocation's output to fixture-pass/expected-annotations.json (empty findings) will fail, permanently breaking the selftest.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 16–18: fixture-pass-policy-check calls policy-check.yml@9928ecc with no with: block. Lines 101–105: fixture-fail-policy-check calls policy-check.yml@9928ecc with no with: block. Both jobs inherit the same github.event.pull_request.base.sha and github.event.pull_request.head.sha. policy-check.yml lines 184–186: git diff --name-only "${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}" > changed-files.txt — identical diff for both invocations. workflow-selftest.yml lines 154–173: normalize() comparison maps first-invocation output to fixture-pass/expected-annotations.json and second to fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json. In 020C, a PR adding policies/*.rego and updating tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml will include fixture-fail/services.yml in changed-files.txt; SCP-R-001 fires on it; both invocations produce the same deny finding; fixture-pass comparison fails. WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md lines 6–9 state 'this fixture's services.yml and expected-annotations.json should change together so the workflow selftest asserts the expected deny summary' — no acknowledgement that fixture-pass comparison simultaneously breaks.
findings.impact: 020C cannot land the described transition (flip fixture-fail to deny) without simultaneously updating fixture-pass/expected-annotations.json to show the same deny — which collapses the fixture-pass / fixture-fail distinction and defeats the harness's stated purpose. The alternative (redesigning fixture isolation to pass per-fixture changed-file sets) requires modifying policy-check.yml (out-of-scope for 020B.1) or adding a new input to differentiate invocations. This is a forward-commitment completeness failure: the documented 020C outcome is unachievable with the committed selftest design. Anti-descoping invariant applies — 020C's AC that fixture-fail asserts deny cannot silently be resolved by making fixture-pass also assert deny.
findings.mitigation: Option A — add a directory-scope input to policy-check.yml (e.g., fixture-root: string, default: '.') that scopes git diff to files under that prefix, then invoke fixture-pass-policy-check with fixture-root: tests/workflow/fixture-pass and fixture-fail-policy-check with fixture-root: tests/workflow/fixture-fail. This requires a minor extension to policy-check.yml (in-scope for a 020B.1 fix round). Option B — split the selftest into two separate workflows, each triggered on its own fixture path and separately checking out the fixture tree. Option C — replace git-diff-based evaluation with whole-tree evaluation (v1.1 input) limited to the fixture directory, invoked with an explicit path arg. Any option must be accompanied by an updated conftest.md explaining the isolation mechanism and updated WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md explaining what specifically changes in 020C. MUST NOT be deferred to 020C since 020C's dispatch package will assume the isolation mechanism is in place.

findings.claim: The expected-annotations oracle files are read from PR HEAD, making the selftest comparison a tautology — an attacker can modify both the fixture services.yml and the expected-annotations.json in the same PR so actual always equals expected, neutralizing the regression gate.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:113-114: actions/checkout at fetch-depth: 1 with no explicit ref, so the working tree is the PR HEAD. workflow-selftest.yml:155-168: normalize(load(expected_path)) reads tests/workflow/fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json from the checked-out tree. normalize() strips pr_sha, base_ref, workflow_run_id but keeps findings, disabled_rules, waivers_applied, bypass_emitted, conflict_gate. An attacker submitting a PR can set fixture-fail/services.yml to a policy-compliant shape and set fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json to {"findings":[],"disabled_rules":[],"waivers_applied":[],"bypass_emitted":false,"conflict_gate":{"run":false,"disagreements":[]}} — both sides of the comparison will then be empty-findings, and assertEqual passes. In 020B.1 both oracle files already contain empty findings so the attack is currently latent; after 020C lands deny findings into fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json the attack becomes critical: an attacker can silently revert that file to all-pass and clean up the fixture services.yml in the same PR.
findings.impact: After 020C, a single PR can strip the deny-finding expectation from fixture-fail without triggering any selftest failure. The self-test provides no structural guarantee that fixture-fail will ever assert a real deny: it only checks that two files the PR author controls are consistent with each other. Every subsequent slice that relies on the selftest to guard policy-check regressions inherits this gap. CODEOWNERS is not yet configured on tests/workflow/** (confirmed: no CODEOWNERS file in repo), so there is currently no compensating review gate.
findings.mitigation: (1) Derive expectations programmatically rather than from a committed oracle: after 020C, assert len(actual["findings"]) >= 1 and actual["findings"][0]["verdict"] == "deny" for the fixture-fail case instead of comparing to a committed JSON file. (2) Or, fetch the expected oracle from the last tagged commit using git show <tag>:tests/workflow/fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json rather than from the PR working tree. (3) Ensure tests/workflow/** is added to CODEOWNERS in slice 020K (currently absent from the enumerated path list in WP-SCP-020 §4 020K) so oracle mutations require a designated reviewer sign-off. Any one of these suffices; (1) plus (3) in combination is strongest.

findings.claim: The hardcoded SHA @9928ecc89f9f90f652f6c10f7a37b1be3e6f9588 in workflow-selftest.yml has no documented maintenance procedure; any future PR modifying policy-check.yml will trigger the selftest (via the .github/workflows/policy-check.yml path trigger) but the selftest will silently validate the stale version at 9928ecc rather than the PR's changed version.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 18 and 105: uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9928ecc89f9f90f652f6c10f7a37b1be3e6f9588. Dispatch package instruction: 'The selftest job MUST use uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<HEAD-SHA>'. The SHA 9928ecc is the dispatch-package commit (git log: '9928ecc WP-SCP-022 slice 020B.1 dispatch package (pre-dispatch evidence)'). Neither conftest.md, WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md, plan §4 020B.1, nor the dispatch-package notes field states that a PR modifying policy-check.yml must simultaneously update this SHA in workflow-selftest.yml. The path trigger .github/workflows/policy-check.yml at workflow-selftest.yml line 6 will cause the selftest to run on any such PR — creating a false-green scenario where the selftest reports success by exercising the old workflow.
findings.impact: Future slices that extend policy-check.yml (e.g., adding a new input or error code) will have the selftest run against the unmodified version, passing trivially while leaving the actual extension untested. The selftest's regression-guard purpose is defeated for any policy-check.yml change made after 9928ecc. The 020C slice adds no policy-check.yml changes, so this doesn't manifest immediately, but it is a live trap for subsequent slices (020C.1 adds waiver-aware Rego and extends the workflow).
findings.mitigation: Add a comment block immediately above each uses: line in workflow-selftest.yml reading: '# PIN: update this SHA whenever policy-check.yml is modified in the same PR. Current pin = 9928ecc (slice 020B.1 dispatch-package commit).' Also add a corresponding note to conftest.md: 'The selftest pins policy-check.yml at a specific commit SHA. Any PR that modifies .github/workflows/policy-check.yml MUST update both occurrences of this SHA in workflow-selftest.yml to the PR head SHA before merging.' Additionally, add a verify_command to the dispatch-package: python3 -c with a check that confirms the two SHA occurrences in workflow-selftest.yml match each other and are non-empty. This does not require redesigning the selftest.

findings.claim: Plan §4 020B.1's scope statement lists only three trigger paths (.github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**) and omits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. The implementation and dispatch-package AC 4 correctly include the fourth path, but the plan text is the governance canonical. Future reviewers auditing 020B.1 conformance against the plan will see a plan-vs-implementation discrepancy with no amendment note.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 row 020B.1: 'SCP-local job workflow-selftest trigger = pull_request on paths .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/** (blocks merge of any PR touching those paths).' — three paths only. workflow-selftest.yml lines 5–9: paths: .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**, schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json — four paths. dispatch-package.json instruction AC 4: explicitly adds schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json as a trigger. The plan §4 is the governing specification per WP-SCP-022 review protocol; the dispatch-package is execution guidance that expanded the AC without amending the plan.
findings.impact: The plan §4 020B.1 row is permanently underspecified relative to the implementation. A future reviewer doing a plan-vs-implementation completeness audit will flag the schema trigger as undocumented scope creep. More critically: if the schema trigger is not in the plan, it is technically unguarded governance — an implementor following the plan alone would omit the schema trigger, creating a CI gap where expected-annotations.json changes silently bypass the selftest.
findings.mitigation: Amend plan §4 020B.1 to add schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json to the trigger path list, with a parenthetical rationale: '(expected-annotations.json is schema-bound; schema changes must re-validate all fixture expectations)'. This is a documentation-only fix to the plan text; the implementation is already correct.

findings.claim: Both `uses:` clauses in workflow-selftest.yml are pegged to SHA `9928ecc` (the pre-implementation dispatch-package commit), not the HEAD commit of the implementing branch (`80d9606`). The AC explicitly requires `@<HEAD-SHA>`.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 18 and 105: `uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9928ecc89f9f90f652f6c10f7a37b1be3e6f9588`. Git log shows HEAD of feature/wp-scp-020b1-workflow-selftest is `80d9606` (WP-SCP-022 slice 020B.1: workflow integration test harness); `9928ecc` is the dispatch-package commit immediately prior, which predates the selftest implementation. Dispatch-package §AC bullet 5: 'invoke the reusable workflow at `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<HEAD-SHA>`'.
findings.impact: The selftest always tests policy-check.yml as it existed at `9928ecc`, not the current branch HEAD. If policy-check.yml is modified in a future PR without bumping this SHA, the selftest silently validates the stale version. There is no automated mechanism (Renovate rule or CI assertion) to detect SHA staleness. For this slice the content is identical so there is no runtime failure, but the invariant is violated.
findings.mitigation: Update both `@9928ecc` values to the HEAD SHA of this branch. For long-term hygiene, add a CI step that asserts the pinned SHA equals the current `github.sha`, OR extend the Renovate `regex-manager` introduced in 020F to also bump the selftest SHA on each merge to main.

findings.claim: Both `fixture-pass-policy-check` and `fixture-fail-policy-check` jobs call policy-check.yml with zero `with:` inputs and no mechanism to target a specific fixture path. policy-check.yml has no fixture-path or services-yml-path input; it evaluates files listed in `git diff base..head`. The two invocations are therefore structurally identical and will always produce the same summary.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 16-18 and 101-105 are bitwise-identical except for job name and `needs`. policy-check.yml `on.workflow_call.inputs` (lines 5-35) defines: rule-set, threshold, annotate, scp_bypass, waivers-path, rule-config-path — no fixture-path parameter. `collect-changed-files` step (policy-check.yml lines 180-186) derives input from `git diff ${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}`. WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md says '020C should change services.yml and expected-annotations.json so the selftest asserts a deny summary' — but with no fixture-path routing, the fixture-fail invocation cannot produce a deny unless `tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml` happens to appear in the PR diff.
findings.impact: In 020B.1 this is masked by the absence of Rego rules — empty findings are expected for both fixtures and both invocations produce them. For 020C, when SCP-R-001/002/003 land, fixture-fail/services.yml must be updated to a non-conformant shape, but the selftest invocation will only evaluate it if that file is in the diff of the PR that adds the rules. Any PR that modifies only the Rego files will invoke the workflow against an empty or unrelated changed-file set and will never evaluate the fixture-fail tree. The self-test harness does not actually provide fixture isolation.
findings.mitigation: 020C must either (a) add a `services-yml-path` input to policy-check.yml and pass the fixture path explicitly in each selftest invocation, or (b) introduce a changed-files override input so the selftest can inject `tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml` as the synthetic changed-file set for the fixture-fail job. This design gap must be documented in WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md before 020C opens, otherwise the 020C implementer will believe only a content change is needed.

findings.claim: The selftest pins policy-check.yml to hardcoded SHA 9928ecc but provides no enforcement that this SHA is updated when policy-check.yml changes; PRs modifying policy-check.yml trigger the selftest but the selftest runs the OLD version, so regressions in the changed workflow are invisible to the gate.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:18: uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9928ecc89f9f90f652f6c10f7a37b1be3e6f9588. workflow-selftest.yml:105: same SHA. The on.pull_request.paths trigger at lines 5-9 includes .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, creating the appearance that changes to policy-check.yml are exercised by the selftest. However, if GitHub honors @<sha> for local reusable workflow refs (GitHub docs state local ./ refs do support SHA pinning), the selftest executes policy-check.yml at commit 9928ecc regardless of what the PR changed. If GitHub does NOT honor it (and always uses the current event SHA), the selftest instead runs the attacker-modified version — which is a separate CRIT vector: a PR that modifies policy-check.yml to remove the SCP_THRESHOLD exit gate (line 391 of policy-check.yml) and sets the expected oracle to all-pass will pass the selftest entirely.
findings.impact: If GitHub honors the SHA: every future PR that modifies policy-check.yml (020C adds OPA/Conftest execution, 020C.1 adds conflict-gate, 020D1 adds the wrapper) bypasses selftest validation of those changes. Regressions in workflow logic go undetected until a canary run in a later slice. If GitHub does NOT honor the SHA: an attacker can modify policy-check.yml to neutralize threshold enforcement (remove sys.exit(1) on line 391) and the selftest will not detect it. Either interpretation constitutes a MAJ gap; the SHA-not-honored case combined with oracle mutability (SBP-001) compounds to CRIT.
findings.mitigation: Add a pre-flight step to workflow-selftest that asserts the SHA embedded in the workflow file matches the current github.sha of policy-check.yml: run `git log -1 --format=%H -- .github/workflows/policy-check.yml` and compare against the hardcoded SHA. Fail the step with an error message directing the author to update the SHA when they change policy-check.yml. This enforces SHA freshness as a mandatory gate. Alternatively, remove the SHA and use ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml without a ref (always current HEAD), then rely on CODEOWNERS on .github/workflows/** (020K) as the mutation gate instead.

findings.claim: The permissions block is declared at workflow level with actions: write, causing all four jobs — including the comparison-only workflow-selftest job — to inherit actions: write. Only stash-fixture-pass-summary requires this permission for artifact deletion. The workflow-selftest job runs inline Python heredocs with access to GITHUB_TOKEN bearing actions: write, unnecessarily elevating blast radius.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:11-13: permissions: actions: write / contents: read at top-level (workflow scope). No per-job permissions override on fixture-pass-policy-check (line 16), fixture-fail-policy-check (line 101), or workflow-selftest (line 107). stash-fixture-pass-summary (lines 20-99) is the only job that needs actions: write — specifically for the GitHub API DELETE call at line 86 (DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/artifacts/{artifact_id}). The workflow-selftest job (lines 107-183) uses GITHUB_TOKEN only implicitly (it does not call the API) but inherits the elevated permission via GITHUB_TOKEN.
findings.impact: If expression injection were achieved in the inline Python at workflow-selftest.yml:136-173 — for example through a future change that reads a PR-controlled value into the Python environment — the attacker would have actions: write capability via GITHUB_TOKEN: artifact deletion (could destroy evidence), workflow cancellation, and run re-queuing. The policy-check.yml reusable workflow also receives actions: write when invoked from this selftest, even though it declares permissions: contents: read at its own level (policy-check.yml:37-38). GitHub does cap the reusable workflow's effective permission at the minimum of the caller-declared and the workflow-declared, so policy-check.yml is safe, but the selftest job itself is not.
findings.mitigation: Remove actions: write from the workflow-level permissions block. Add a job-level permissions block to stash-fixture-pass-summary: `permissions: actions: write` and `contents: read`. Set `permissions: contents: read` explicitly on fixture-pass-policy-check, fixture-fail-policy-check, and workflow-selftest jobs. This restores minimum-privilege per job.

findings.claim: conftest.md does not document that workflow-selftest.yml pins policy-check.yml at a specific commit SHA, nor that a PR modifying policy-check.yml must update that SHA in the same PR. As the harness README, conftest.md is the first document a future developer will read when editing the test setup.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/conftest.md (all 11 lines): describes fixture purpose and slice-020C transition note. No mention of the @SHA pin in workflow-selftest.yml, the maintenance requirement, or the risk of stale-SHA false-greens. The conftest.md's slice-020C section mentions only that 'services.yml and expected-annotations.json will diverge' — it does not mention the SHA update requirement that will accompany any workflow change.
findings.impact: A developer extending the harness in a post-020B.1 slice who reads conftest.md as orientation will not be warned of the SHA maintenance requirement. Combined with CG-MAJ-01, this increases the likelihood of a stale-SHA false-green scenario.
findings.mitigation: Add a 'Maintenance notes' section to conftest.md with two bullets: (1) 'workflow-selftest.yml pins policy-check.yml at a commit SHA. Update both occurrences when policy-check.yml changes in the same PR.' (2) 'When 020C updates fixture-fail/services.yml to carry a deliberate violation, both services.yml files and their expected-annotations.json partners must be updated together — and the fixture isolation mechanism (see CG-CRIT-01 resolution) must be in place before this flip.' This fix depends on CG-CRIT-01 being resolved first so the isolation mechanism is known.

findings.claim: The fixture-fail-policy-check job (workflow-selftest.yml lines 101–105) has no structural differentiation from fixture-pass-policy-check: no with: block, no comment indicating which fixture it targets, and no marker that the 020C extension requires a redesign of isolation rather than a naive expected-annotations.json flip.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 101–105: fixture-fail-policy-check: name: fixture-fail-policy-check, needs: stash-fixture-pass-summary, uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9928ecc — identical structure to fixture-pass-policy-check (lines 16–18) except for the name and needs fields. The only 020C reference in the workflow is a comment at line 104 ('020C flips this fixture to a deny assertion once SCP-R-001/002/003 land') and the workflow summary at lines 182–183. Neither comment acknowledges that the flip requires an isolation mechanism redesign; both imply a simple expected-annotations.json update suffices.
findings.impact: A developer implementing 020C will read the comment at line 104 as authorisation to update fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json and assume the selftest will then pass. This masks CG-CRIT-01 until 020C's selftest run fails. The misleading comment is a forward-descoping risk embedded in the governance document trail.
findings.mitigation: Replace the line 104 comment with: '# 020C: DO NOT simply flip expected-annotations.json here. The two invocations share identical PR context and produce identical outputs. Fixture isolation must be resolved (see CG-CRIT-01 in review-completeness.json) before 020C can implement the deny assertion.' This prevents a naive 020C implementation from silently descoping the isolation requirement.

findings.claim: The stash-fixture-pass-summary job lists run artifacts via `GET /runs/{run_id}/artifacts` with no `per_page` parameter and no pagination loop. GitHub API defaults to 30 items per page. The subsequent assertion `len(matches) != 1` will spuriously fail with 'found 0' if more than 30 artifacts exist in the run and the `policy-check-summary` artifact falls on page 2.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 62-79: `urllib.request.Request(f"{api_url}/repos/{repository}/actions/runs/{run_id}/artifacts", headers=headers)` followed by `payload.get('artifacts', [])` with no Link-header pagination. GitHub REST API documentation: default page size = 30.
findings.impact: Unlikely to trigger in normal SCP repo operation with a small number of artifacts per run. However, if run retries or concurrent matrix jobs accumulate artifacts, the stash step could fail non-deterministically with a misleading 'found 0 artifacts' error rather than the real cause. This would block the selftest without a clear diagnosis path.
findings.mitigation: Append `?per_page=100` to the artifact list URL. For full correctness add a pagination loop that follows the `Link` response header until no `next` rel is present.

findings.claim: fixture-pass/services.yml uses jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json as a placeholder. When SCP-R-001 ships in 020C and validates services.yml root-shape, if the rule enforces jwks_url domain format or reachability, example.com (an IANA-reserved placeholder domain) will produce a deny finding on the fixture-pass fixture — causing fixture-pass to fail and bricking the selftest permanently.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-pass/services.yml:16: jwks_url: https://example.com/.well-known/jwks.json. WP-SCP-020 §4 020C: SCP-R-001 validates root-shape conformance to pre-D-021 SVC-003 mode set; the plan text does not enumerate which sub-fields of accepted_modes are validated beyond mode enum membership. The fixture-fail services.yml (line 16) uses the same placeholder. If both fixtures use a URL that fails SCP-R-001, both produce deny findings — fixture-pass breaks and the selftest cannot distinguish the two cases.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 validates jwks_url beyond URI format (e.g., domain must match *.brokapps.ai or *.anthropic.com, or must be reachable), the selftest will permanently fail after 020C merge, blocking all downstream slices (020C.1, 020J, 020K, 020D1) which share the same branch. The 020C author must audit this before landing. No mitigation is pre-wired — the conftest.md and WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md do not mention jwks_url validation scope.
findings.mitigation: Before 020C opens, explicitly document in the SCP-R-001 rule spec whether jwks_url is validated for format only (URI string) or also for domain/reachability. If domain validation is in scope, replace example.com in both fixture files with a URL pattern that will always pass the rule (e.g., https://auth.brokapps.example/.well-known/jwks.json using a well-known test TLD, or a synthetic constant like https://fixture.scp-selftest.internal/jwks.json). Add a note to conftest.md documenting this invariant.

findings.claim: tests/workflow/** is absent from the planned CODEOWNERS paths enumerated in slice 020K. Once 020C promotes fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json to contain real deny findings, that file becomes a security-relevant oracle, but it will have no designated reviewer gate at PR merge time.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-020 §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list: policies/**, renovate/**, .github/workflows/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, output/findings/waivers.json. tests/workflow/** is not in this list. Confirmed: no CODEOWNERS file exists in the repository (glob returned no results). dispatch-package.json scope_boundary includes tests/workflow/** but scope_boundary is an implementation scope marker, not a CODEOWNERS pointer.
findings.impact: Without CODEOWNERS on tests/workflow/**, any collaborator can modify the oracle files in a PR and have it merge without a designated-reviewer review. Combined with SBP-001 (mutable oracle), this means no human review gate compensates for the structural tautology gap. The window of exposure is from 020C merge (when the oracle becomes meaningful) until 020K landing — which, per the slice order, is several slices later.
findings.mitigation: Add tests/workflow/** to the CODEOWNERS path list in slice 020K. Update the 020K acceptance criteria to enumerate this path explicitly. Consider noting this gap in the WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md or conftest.md so the 020C author is prompted to address it at 020K.

findings.claim: WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md uses 'should' (permissive) for a transition that plan §4 020B.1 treats as a required AC of 020C.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-fail/WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md lines 6–9: 'this fixture's services.yml and expected-annotations.json **should** change together so the workflow selftest asserts the expected deny summary.' Plan §4 020C: 'fixture-fail/ tree exists but is structurally identical to fixture-pass/ … the selftest workflow will then assert a deny-shaped summary for that fixture' — no 'should', imperative framing. Governance docs use 'must' for required transitions per estate convention.
findings.impact: Trivial in isolation; combined with CG-MIN-02's misleading comment, the permissive language gives a 020C implementor multiple off-ramps to interpret the fixture flip as optional.
findings.mitigation: Replace 'should' with 'must' in WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md line 6. Also add: 'Note: the two selftest invocations must be isolated by fixture directory before this flip can succeed — see CG-CRIT-01 resolution notes.'

findings.claim: The `normalize()` function in the workflow-selftest comparison step silently drops `pr_sha`, `base_ref`, and `workflow_run_id` from both actual and expected payloads. The expected-annotations.json files carry stub values (`pr_sha: '000...0'`, `workflow_run_id: 0`) that are required by the schema but are never actually compared. A maintainer updating expected-annotations.json could change these stub values and believe they have tightened the assertion; the change has no effect.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 143-151 (normalize body): keys schema_version, rule_set, findings, disabled_rules, waivers_applied, bypass_emitted, conflict_gate — pr_sha, base_ref, workflow_run_id absent. expected-annotations.json lines 3 and 6 carry placeholder values.
findings.impact: Low. No runtime correctness regression. However, correctness regressions in `pr_sha` or `workflow_run_id` (e.g., empty string or wrong format slipping through) would not be caught by the selftest comparison.
findings.mitigation: Add a brief inline comment in both expected-annotations.json files stating that `pr_sha` and `workflow_run_id` are schema-required stubs not used in comparison. Alternatively, include them in `normalize()` and compare them as pattern-assertions (e.g., assert pr_sha matches `[0-9a-f]{40}` and workflow_run_id is a positive integer) rather than exact value equality.

findings.claim: WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md describes only a content change to services.yml and expected-annotations.json as the 020C requirement. It does not mention that the selftest workflow itself requires structural changes to provide fixture-path isolation (see COR-002). A future implementer reading only this file would underestimate the 020C scope.
findings.evidence: WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md lines 7-9: 'this fixture's services.yml and expected-annotations.json should change together so the workflow selftest asserts the expected deny summary instead of today's empty findings payload.' No mention of workflow-selftest.yml changes.
findings.impact: Scope underestimate for 020C. Discoverable at 020C planning time, but creates rework risk if not flagged now.
findings.mitigation: Add a second paragraph to WILL-FAIL-AFTER-020C.md noting that workflow-selftest.yml also requires a fixture-path routing mechanism (e.g., a new `services-yml-path` input on policy-check.yml) before the fixture-fail invocation can produce a non-empty findings summary.

findings.claim: The hardcoded SHA comment on uses: lines does not document its purpose, update procedure, or whether GitHub honors @<sha> for local ./ workflow refs. Future maintainers have no in-code signal that failing to update the SHA when modifying policy-check.yml creates a regression gap.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:18: `uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9928ecc89f9f90f652f6c10f7a37b1be3e6f9588` — no comment. Compare with actions/download-artifact lines (e.g., line 26: `uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0`) which include a human-readable version comment. The policy-check.yml SHA lacks even a version annotation.
findings.impact: No direct security impact. Maintenance overhead: a future slice author may not realize they must update this SHA when changing policy-check.yml, reinforcing the regression gap in SBP-002.
findings.mitigation: Add an inline comment: `# policy-check.yml at commit 9928ecc (020B.1 dispatch package); update this SHA and confirm selftest passes whenever policy-check.yml changes.`

findings.claim: The artifact stash-rename-delete ceremony between the two fixture invocations relies on GitHub artifact API eventual consistency; if the DELETE response is delayed in propagation, the second invocation's upload of policy-check-summary may encounter a name collision, and the workflow-selftest comparison job may download the wrong artifact for fixture-fail.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml:38-99: stash-fixture-pass-summary deletes the artifact named policy-check-summary after renaming it to fixture-pass-policy-check-summary. The Python script validates len(matches) == 1 before deleting (lines 74-79) but does not verify propagation after the 204 DELETE response. workflow-selftest.yml:101-105: fixture-fail-policy-check runs with needs: stash-fixture-pass-summary — sequential dependency is correct, but GitHub artifact propagation latency is not gated.
findings.impact: Very low probability under normal conditions. If the DELETE propagates late, the fixture-fail invocation's artifact upload may fail or overwrite the stashed copy. The workflow-selftest download step (line 127) reads name: policy-check-summary and would receive the fixture-fail artifact correctly if upload succeeded; the risk is upload failure causing if-no-files-found: error on the second invocation, failing the run with a confusing error rather than a logic bypass. Not a security vulnerability, but a fragility in the coordination mechanism.
findings.mitigation: Eliminate the stash-rename-delete ceremony by adding a fixture-id input to policy-check.yml (e.g., artifact-name-suffix: string, default: policy-check-summary) so each invocation uploads to a distinct artifact name (fixture-pass-policy-check-summary and fixture-fail-policy-check-summary directly). This removes the sequential coordination dependency entirely.
